coaching.summary: The graph captures the core tension well but leaves the reliability-to-revenue causal chain underspecified, which is exactly the chain the board will interrogate. Strengthening the quantitative links and surfacing the time-lag between engineering hires and reliability improvement will sharpen the Q3 ARR argument.

strengthen_items.label: Quantify the reliability-debt-to-churn link
strengthen_items.detail: Attach a numeric estimate (e.g., current churn rate attributable to reliability failures) to the edge from Platform Reliability Debt to Customer Churn from Reliability Failures so the board can see the revenue-at-risk baseline before any hire is made.

strengthen_items.label: Add a time-to-impact constraint for engineering hires
strengthen_items.detail: Platform engineers hired in Q1 are unlikely to reduce reliability debt and churn before Q3; making this lag explicit as a constraint on Platform Reliability Improvement prevents the split or eng-only option from being oversold as a Q3 ARR lever.

strengthen_items.label: Clarify what ARR growth threshold satisfies the board
strengthen_items.detail: Achieve ARR Growth by Q3 is currently binary; specifying a target percentage or dollar figure turns it into a testable criterion and reveals whether any option can realistically hit it by Q3 given current churn and quota-miss rates.

strengthen_items.label: Trace how reliability improvement reduces quota miss
strengthen_items.detail: Add an explicit edge from Platform Reliability Improvement to Sales Quota Miss Due to Product Gaps to capture the brief's stated fact that AEs already miss quota because of product reliability, making the indirect revenue benefit of engineering hires visible in the graph.

elements_considered_but_excluded: Recruiting timeline node — relevant but adds complexity without changing the option set
Competitive pressure node — mentioned implicitly via Market Demand for Product, not distinct enough to add

bias_signals.detail: The graph treats Platform Reliability Improvement as a direct path to Achieve ARR Growth by Q3 without encoding the multi-month lag between hiring engineers and measurable reliability gains, risking an overly optimistic Q3 forecast.

The board's stated focus on ARR growth may anchor the decision toward Hire Three Account Executives even though the brief explicitly says AEs cannot close deals due to reliability issues, making the sales-only option less viable than it appears.

Framing the choice as three discrete options plus status quo may suppress hybrid sequencing strategies (e.g., two engineers now, two AEs in Q2 contingent on reliability milestones) that the current graph structure cannot represent.
